newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - July 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - July 23.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- ASEAN has failed to resolve sharp differences over Cambodia on the eve of the scheduled admission of Burma and Laos. Some members, such as Vietnam, want a joint communique on Friday explaining the hold-up to take a positive tone while others, including the Philippines and Singapore, feel it should reflect the realities in Cambodia. (BANGKOK POST, THE NATION)

- The inclusion of a ban on MPs and senators holding cabinet positions is expected to result in the death of the draft constitution in Parliament. The Constitution Drafting Assembly voted yesterday to retain Article 205, under which MPs and senators would lose their parliamentary status if appointed as ministers or prime minister. (BANGKOK POST, THE NATION)

- Dozens of tourists have been trapped in a forest reserve by flash floods and the overflowing of Noi River in two districts of Kanchanaburi province. Torrential monsoon rains in the past few days have caused sudden flooding in areas surrounding the forest, which is a popular tourist attraction boasting a bat cave and scenic waterways used for rafting. (THE NATION)

- The Commerce Ministry expects prices of consumer products under 30 categories to increase very soon because the manufacturers are shouldering a five percent increase in produciton cost due to the baht value which has already tumbled by around 15 percent. (BUSINESS DAY)

- In an abrupt about-face, Bangkok Bank has reversed last week's decision to increase fixed deposit interest rates by as much as 250 basis points, citing a slight misunderstanding. Other large banks, with the exception of third-ranked Thai Farmers, quickly scrapped plans to follow the market leader. But deposit rates will likely rise again soon since local banks, effectively cut off from foreign funds, are scrambling to attract cash. (BANGKOK POST)
